The design is controlled via input pins and provides DAC control signals and 8-bit data outputs. The documentation is minimal, providing only the pin list and a one-line description, so detailed operation and testing are not described.

results.summary_before: This project implements the PRESENT block cipher with a hardware trojan that can inject faults. It has an 8-bit data input, 8-bit data output, and command inputs via bidirectional pins. The design is tested with functional tests from OpenCores and additional tests for encryption rounds with fixed key and plaintext to verify fault behavior. The hardware trojan is a deliberate malicious modification, making this a security research project.

results.summary_before: This project is an 8-bit CPU implemented in Verilog that performs arithmetic and load instructions and outputs the result of each instruction on eight output pins. It exposes an eight-bit input bus, a status pin, reset, clock, instruction enable, and four program counter bits on the bidirectional pins. Testing is done with a script that simulates the instruction register, waiting for the microcontroller to request a program counter value and returning the allocated instruction, allowing custom assembly programs to be swapped quickly. The documentation is a proposal-level description and does not detail the full instruction set or verified behavior.

results.summary_before: This project implements a 2-layer binary neural network (BNN) that classifies an 8-bit input into one of four categories (turn left, turn right, stop, U-turn). It uses XNOR-popcount operations instead of multipliers, and supports real-time weight loading via a 4-bit bidirectional interface. The design is intended for educational and demonstrational purposes, showing simple ML on-chip without CPUs or RAM. Testing is done with CocoTB, and accuracy is limited due to the small network size.
results.summary: This project implements an 8-LED choreographer that generates patterns such as Knight Rider, waves, and sparkles. It operates on a 5MHz system clock and uses a built-in clock divider to provide two speed modes: fast mode updates patterns at 4Hz and slow mode at 1Hz. The design has inputs for pattern selection, speed selection, pause, and enable, and outputs to eight LEDs. The documentation describes the clocking and speed modes but does not detail all available patterns or testing.
